# Electrical Docs


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This site covers electricity on paper, in data, and in the equipment that carries it. It starts with the equations and circuit theory, works through three-phase power systems, single line diagrams and control, then moves to filters and signal processing, forecasts grid load from real demand data, and asks whether a home battery pays for itself. It ends with the practical kit: the electrical toolbox, what a switchboard contains, and the motor families. The newer pages are runnable: each works an example in code and checks it with assertions.

For microcontrollers, builds and industrial automation see [Hardware Tools](https://bthek1.github.io/Hardware_Tools/). For the general forecasting toolkit these pages build on see [Time Series ML](https://bthek1.github.io/ML_Timeseries/).

## Signals and Forecasting

| Page | Covers |
|----|----|
| [Filter Design](08_Filter_Design.ipynb) | Pulling a 5 Hz signal out of 50 Hz hum and noise: RC filters, order and the Butterworth, Chebyshev and Bessel families, aliasing, and FIR against IIR filters, including the cost of delay |
| [FFT Examples](09_FFT_Examples.ipynb) | Forecasting strongly seasonal series with the Darts FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) model, improved step by step by cropping, filtering low-amplitude waves and detrending, then applied to hourly nuclear generation |

## Motors

Four pages, one per family, each covering how it works, how it is driven, and how to program it. Read [Electric Motors](Electrical_Motors/01_Electric_Motors.ipynb) first for the map.

| Page | Covers |
|----|----|
| [Electric Motors](Electrical_Motors/01_Electric_Motors.ipynb) | The overview. How a motor converts current into motion, the DC, AC, and special families, drivers and control, the specifications that matter, and how to pick one for a job |
| [Servo Motors](Electrical_Motors/02_Servos.ipynb) | Closed-loop actuators that hold a commanded position. Hobby servo anatomy and PWM control, then industrial servos with encoders, drives, tuning, and motion profiles |
| [Stepper Motors](Electrical_Motors/03_Stepper_Motors.ipynb) | Open-loop precision. Bipolar against unipolar coils, step modes and microstepping, and step/direction driver control |
| [Brushless Motors](Electrical_Motors/04_Brushless_Motors.ipynb) | BLDC and PMSM: electronic commutation in place of brushes, rotor position sensing, and the ESC that makes it all work |

## Not Covered Yet

- **No power electronics.** Nothing on rectifiers, buck and boost converters or inverters, which are what connect solar panels and batteries to the three-phase grid.
- **No circuit transients.** RC, RL and RLC step responses, and the switching surges they cause, appear only indirectly through the motor model in Control Systems.
- **No test and measurement page.** Oscilloscopes and logic analysers are named in the tools list but never explained.
- **No protection grading.** The SLD page computes fault levels, but nothing covers fuse and breaker time-current curves or how upstream and downstream devices are coordinated.
